topScam.title: The Fake Google Customer Care & Screen Share Hijack
topScam.scam: When searching for Swiggy, Zomato, IRCTC, or bank customer support on Google, users dial a fake number placed by scammers. The fake agent says: "To process your ₹200 refund, share your screen on WhatsApp video call or install AnyDesk/QuickSupport." Once screen sharing starts, the scammer initiates a bank transfer and reads the incoming OTP directly off the live screen.
topScam.protection: Never search for customer service phone numbers on Google Search; always use the in-app help section. Never share your mobile screen or accept screen-sharing requests during a customer support call.
topScam.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Sachet Advisory)

realityPick.title: The Structured JSON Illusion
realityPick.myth: Just tell the LLM to output valid JSON matching your schema — instant API integration!
realityPick.reality: Under latency pressure or novel input tokens, LLMs will prepend conversational preamble, output trailing commas, or truncate JSON arrays when nearing token limits, breaking downstream backend parsers.
realityPick.fix: Never rely on raw prompting for JSON. Use constrained grammar sampling at the model engine level (forcing logits to only output valid schema tokens).
realityPick.impact: Downstream checkout or database ingestion services crash silently in production due to an unescaped double-quote or missing closing brace.
